quotes.text: For both the Israelites and the Saints, their travail forged great spiritual strength. They both endured trials of their faith during which the weak were winnowed away and the strong were empowered to endure to the end (see Ether 12:6; D&C 101:4-5; 105:19). They had to leave their homes and earthly possessions and learn to rely wholly upon God. Protection was provided for ancient Israel by the Lord, who "went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire" (Exodus 13:21; see also v. 22; Numbers 14:14; Deuteronomy 1:33; Nehemiah 9:19). The same has been said of divine watchcare afforded to the pioneers (see History of the Church, 3:xxxiv; Thomas S. Monson, in Conference Report, Apr. 1967, 56).

notes.text: George Reynolds and Janne M. Sjodahl, Commentary on the Pearl of Great Price). "Near Eastern literature, not just Hebrew, reveals a fondness for using numbers to communicate ideas. Why certain numbers became laden with symbolic meaning is unknown; in most cases this arose in prehistoric times and is now lost to us. Interestingly there is a general consistency across cultures to the meaning of certain numbers. That is not to say that numbers are never used as numbers. Certainly they mostly signify only literal quantity. However, in certain contexts they express ideas… One should interpret numbers just as the other symbolic representations". (Richard D. Draper, Opening the Seven Seals: The Visions of John the Revelator, 23.) Here is a short list of numbers and their symbolic meaning. [A strong caution - this is not a 'secret decoder' - no scripture is of private interpretation (2 Peter 1:20)].Some possible meanings are: One = deity or God; two = division or opposition; three = covenant; four = earth or man; five = atonement or grace; six = incomplete or evil; seven = complete or whole; eight = new beginning; nine = judgment; ten = divine completeness or hand of God; twelve = priesthood government; forty = time of preparation (For more examples see Sterling W.
